headline: V26-3645: checks as a workflow component, so a lane's recorded pass counts and guards run where a change is checked

V26-3660.title: Run a check the way the queue does, anywhere, with the facts that make it reproducible

criteria.text: run-checks writes one record per id with every field above, exits non-zero on a failure with its log kept, and never prints a variable's value.

A variable outside the baseline and inherit doesn't reach a check in the queue or in run-checks; the failure output names dropped variables; listing it in inherit makes it pass; the runner's own git keeps the inherited environment.
run-checks from a second worktree, with different TMPDIR and PATH, yields the same environment digest and host facts as the queue from the main checkout.
run-checks and a queue command sharing a --repo both finish without removing each other's worktree.
handoff --evidence accepts and keeps the widened fields and still accepts the five-field shape.
No fixed rule replaces the agent's judgement: the facts are recorded, and nothing is refused on them here.

V26-3661.title: Answer whether a recorded pass applies, and reuse a lane's pass by default

criteria.text: Every existing reusable and carry_plan outcome holds after both call applies, and a pre-change queue row with no facts still carries.

A lane record applies at an identical tree, across an unread base move, and across a move outside a complete read set; it runs with a named reason for a move inside the read set, an unknown read set, differing facts (value, swapped values, tool, platform, where: checkout), missing facts, a changed definition, a failure, a needed prerequisite, a binding change, an exclusion or a {baseHead} placeholder. Notes never print a value.

A grant makes the V26-3614 shape apply (record before a lane-side base merge, handed head the merge, unknown read set) and journals check.reused with because; it doesn't apply after a lane change or a revert to a path the candidate touched, after a new hand-off, or for a checkout, differing-facts, changed-definition or failed record.
No fixed rule replaces the agent's judgement: reuse is the default when applies says so, and the grant is the recorded override.

V26-3662.title: Record a lane's check runs, and hand off with them

criteria.text: check writes records equal to what run-checks prints, at HEAD.
A later failing record replaces an earlier pass in the hand-off.
An id gate leaves a runner record and an inline gate a checkout record; gates_summary behaves as before.

End to end: in a child process whose TMPDIR and PATH differ from the queue's, a lane runs check in its worktree and hands off, and a queue run from the main checkout at the same tree reuses the record and journals check.reused.
No fixed rule replaces the agent's judgement: nothing is refused for a missing record.

V26-3664.title: Run guards where a change is checked, and show the lead what still applies

criteria.text: In a fixture binding, a diff its guard rejects fails gate, naming the guard, before the repository's gates run; a second gate at the same tree reuses the pass; a recorded skip shows in the hand-off and gates_summary still passes.

lead-push publishes with no override when guards pass at the published commit, journaling no decision.recorded; refuses and publishes nothing when a guard rejects a merge whose parents each pass; publishes with --skip-guards --why and journals decision.recorded.
lead-accept's proposal shows applies or why not and the median for each selected check, and --reuse records the grant.
No fixed rule replaces the agent's judgement: every default has a --why override, and only lead-push refuses.

V26-3663.title: Start guards first and the longest checks next

criteria.text: The start order follows the rule above.
A failing guard ends the run before any other check starts.
A passing run records the same results as before.
No fixed rule replaces the agent's judgement: ordering changes nothing about which checks run.

outOfScope: **What no record can capture.** That means nondeterminism (network, clock, randomness, concurrency and flaky tests), external services, and programs a check calls that neither its argv nor `reuse.tools` names. These stay what `fullHealth` catches after a merge. The queue's own runs share every one of them, so reuse adds no gap beyond the queue's own.
Declaring read sets or `unread` paths for this repository's catalogue. Decision 5 covers V26-3614's case without them, and which paths are truly unread is a judgement for a later change.
Inferring read sets from imports or file access.
Keeping a prepared runner worktree between runs. Each run prepares afresh, as the queue does, and commands show the prepare time.
Running guards inside `review-prepare` or `lead-accept`. Both show the guard records.
Formatting (V26-3652), shared-machine capacity (V26-3638), and any change to the TypeScript harness.
Changing the existing `handoff` refusal when the gates haven't passed at the head.
